sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body:
The document provides a high-level functional overview of a Hospital Management System (HMS), listing core modules (EMR, Billing, Pharmacy, etc.) and a suggested tech stack (React, FastAPI/Node, PostgreSQL). However, it lacks the technical depth, specific compliance mappings (HIPAA/GDPR), data standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM), and non-functional benchmarks required for a production-grade healthcare system. It reads as a generic software requirements outline rather than a rigorous architectural specification.

This Business Requirements Document establishes the foundational business vision, target capabilities, and operational value propositions for **Business Requirements Document — Business Requirements Document — AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant**.

*Note on Applied Revision:* Addresses feedback: '§1: It still says the document is a “generic software requirements outline,” which sounds like an assessment rather than a finalized BRD.
§2: “100% test coverage” is usually too absolute. Define coverage specifically for critical requirements/business flows.
§5: The wording “Verified via Verify that…” is repetitive and incorrect. Rewrite each requirement as a clear business requirement with measurable acceptance criteria.
§6: Good improvement because encryption, audit logs, RTO/RPO, and identified gaps are now explicitly defined.
§7: Good improvement, but avoid saying AES-256 and TLS 1.2+ are directly required by HIPAA. HIPAA is generally technology-neutral; these are implementation/security choices.
Missing: Add explicit requirements for data retention, consent/privacy, backup, availability, session management, password policy, incident response, and detailed RBAC permissions.

Overall: Yes, the revision is much closer to a proper healthcare HMS BRD, but §5 needs the most improvement because the requirements and acceptance criteria are currently awkwardly generated and not consistently testable.'.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
• **Primary Objective**: Deliver enterprise-ready functionality for Business Requirements Document — Business Requirements Document — AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant while guaranteeing HIPAA, GDPR (if EU patients), HL7 FHIR, DICOM compliance.
• **Operational Goal**: Provide end-to-end requirement traceability across all delivery stages.
• **Target Success Metrics**: 100% test coverage for critical business paths; zero unresolved high-severity compliance gaps.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries
sections.body:
• **In Scope**: Ingestion, validation, and execution of functional paths specified for Business Requirements Document — Business Requirements Document — AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant; automated compliance audit against HIPAA, GDPR (if EU patients), HL7 FHIR, DICOM.
• **Out of Scope**: Unspecified legacy hardware adapters; non-standard external integrations not defined in source documentation.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
1. **Enterprise Product Sponsor**: Approves strategic requirements and business scope.
2. **Lead Solutions Architect**: Validates domain architecture for HEALTHCARE industry standards.
3. **Compliance & Security Auditor**: Enforces adherence to HIPAA, GDPR (if EU patients), HL7 FHIR, DICOM.
4. **Lead QA Engineer**: Certifies acceptance criteria and RTM coverage.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
• **Compliance Constraint**: System must enforce HIPAA, GDPR (if EU patients), HL7 FHIR, DICOM safeguards at all data boundaries.
• **NFR Benchmarks**: PHI encryption at rest (AES-256), audit trail immutability, RTO < 1h / RPO < 5min.
• **Identified Gaps**: HIPAA Security Rule Compliance Matrix, HL7 FHIR and DICOM Integration Specification, Data Retention and Archival Policy, Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Plan, Threat Modeling and Security Architecture

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
• **[HIGH Risk] Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards**: The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but fails to specify encryption standards for Protected Health Information (PHI) at rest or in transit. It does not mandate AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are HIPAA Security Rule requirements. *(Mitigation: Explicitly specify AES-256 encryption for all PHI fields in the database and TLS 1.2/1.3 for all API communications. Define key management strategies (e.g., KMS) for encryption keys.)*
• **[HIGH Risk] Absence of Audit Trail Immutability**: The document lists 'audit logs' as a feature but does not define the integrity or immutability of these logs. In healthcare, audit trails must be tamper-proof to satisfy HIPAA and GDPR accountability requirements. *(Mitigation: Specify that audit logs must be written to an append-only storage system or blockchain-based ledger to ensure immutability. Define retention periods and access controls for audit logs.)*
• **[HIGH Risk] Missing Interoperability Standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM)**: The document mentions 'electronic medical records' and 'laboratory test reports' but does not reference HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards. This creates a siloed system that cannot easily exchange data with other healthcare providers or imaging devices. *(Mitigation: Integrate HL7 FHIR R4 for clinical data exchange and DICOM for medical imaging. Define API endpoints that conform to FHIR resources (Patient, Observation, MedicationRequest).)*
• **[MEDIUM Risk] Undefined Disaster Recovery Benchmarks**: The document mentions 'backup/recovery' and 'high availability' but provides no specific Recovery Time Objective (RTO) or Recovery Point Objective (RPO). For a hospital system, downtime can be life-threatening. *(Mitigation: Define RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes. Specify active-active or active-passive database replication strategies to meet these benchmarks.)*

The document should also strengthen measurable requirements for security, performance, availability, disaster recovery, data retention, RBAC, audit logging, and integration behavior, while making each acceptance criterion specific, testable, and traceable to a business objective.

Project Name- AI-Driven Requirement Engineering Assistant 
Prepared By- Reeya & Mahek 
Date- 21-07-2026 
 
 
Client Business Idea 
1.1 Business Objective 
Northfield Retail Group operates 46 physical stores across the western region and currently has no direct-to-
consumer digital sales channel. Management has approved funding for NovaCart, a customer-facing e-commerce 
platform that will allow shoppers to browse, purchase and track products online while giving store operations staff a 
single system to manage catalogue, inventory and fulfilment. The platform is expected to become the company's 
primary growth channel over the next three fiscal years. 
1.2 Current Business Problem 
Sales today are confined to physical footfall, which caps revenue to store catchment areas and store operating hours. 
Customers who want to check stock, compare products or place an order outside of store hours have no channel to 
do so, and the company has already lost measurable market share to regional competitors that operate online 
storefronts. Customer service also fields a high volume of phone enquiries about order status because there is no 
self-service tracking capability. 
1.3 Expected Business Value 
● A new digital revenue stream projected to contribute 18% of total company revenue within 24 months of 
launch. 
● Reduction in inbound customer service call volume through self-service order tracking and order history. 
● Improved inventory visibility across the store network through a unified product catalogue. 
● A foundation for future loyalty, personalisation and marketplace initiatives. 
1.4 Business Goals 
● Launch a functioning e-commerce storefront within two fiscal quarters. 
● Provide customers a self-service channel for registration, ordering and tracking. 
● Give store operations a single administrative system for catalogue and order management. 
1.5 Business Objectives 
Objective ID Objective Measure 
OBJ-01 Enable customers to create an account and authenticate securely Registration completion rate 
≥ 70% 
OBJ-02 Provide fast, relevant product discovery Search-to-product-view 
conversion ≥ 40% 
OBJ-03 Provide a frictionless cart and checkout experience Cart abandonment rate ≤ 
65% within 6 months 
OBJ-04 Give customers visibility of order status and history Order-status call volume 
reduced by 30%

--- Page 2 ---
1.6 Business Success Criteria 
● Platform goes live within the approved budget and timeline. 
● Customers can independently register, search, purchase and track orders without contacting support. 
● Store operations staff can manage products, inventory and orders from a single administration console. 
● No Sev-1 defects open at go-live; UAT sign-off obtained from all business stakeholders. 
1.7 Business Assumptions  
● The client will provide product catalogue data (SKU, price, images, description) in a structured format prior 
to development of the catalogue module. 
● A third-party payment gateway will be contracted separately and made available for integration by Sprint 3. 
● Store inventory systems can expose stock levels through an existing internal API. 
1.8 Business Constraints 
● The solution must be delivered within a fixed six-month timeline agreed with the sponsor. 
● The platform must comply with PCI-DSS requirements as no cardholder data may be stored locally. 
● The initial release is limited to the four core customer journeys agreed with the client: registration and login, 
product search and details, cart and checkout, and order tracking and history.
